newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Power gets gas transporter licence.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Power gets gas transporter licence.

text.p: Scottish Power Plc said on Thursday it was granted a gas transporter licence by British gas watchdog OFGAS so it can now provide gas pipelines for property and commercial developments throughout the UK.
The company said the license is a further step in positioning the it to own and install a package of electricity, gas, telecommunications and water infrastructure services.

"The gas transporter licence allows us to compete for new business in an expanding market for both large and small-scale gas installation," said Duncan Whyte, Scottish Power Executive Director, Multi Utility.

As part of it drive to compete in the newly liberated domestic supply business, Scottish Power has currently supplying 70,000 customers in the recent gas trials in Kent and Sussex, part of the region served by its Southern Water subsidiary.
Ofgas recently said natural gas customers are leaving the former monopoly supplier in search of cheaper alternatives at the rate of over 1,000 a day.

A total of 302,823 consumers have now left British Gas Trading (BGT), formerly part of monopoly supplier British Gas plc, out of a total of 2.2 million potential customers. This represents around 14 percent of the total.

Domestic gas competition has been introduced in phases, with Devon, Somerset and Cornwall opening up last April. A second phase followed with Avon and Dorset opening in February this year and Kent and East and West Sussex in March.
Ofgas hopes to see competition introduced in Scotland and North East England this autumn, and to the rest of the country by April 1998.
Scottish Power's first major infrastructure project under the gas transporter licence will be to install new gas services to a major industrial and housing expansion in Dunfermline in Fife.
The gas infrastructure is being installed in the same trench as the electricity and telecoms services that Scottish Power is also providing to the site. Work is due for completion by October.
